claims.text: Elevated-temperature degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is governed by diffusion-controlled selective oxidation.
Under oxidizing conditions, Al, Cr, and Ti preferentially diffuse to the alloy surface.
Preferential diffusion of Al, Cr, and Ti under oxidizing conditions produces a continuous, compositionally complex oxide scale.
The continuous oxide scale protects the fcc matrix and limits further degradation.
Under H2-rich reducing conditions, oxide-scale formation is incomplete or patchy.
Incomplete or patchy oxide formation under reducing conditions accelerates degradation.
The as-built alloy has a uniform fcc matrix with minimal processing-induced heterogeneity.
The as-built alloy has demonstrated notable strength and fatigue performance.
Oxide scales form and evolve along grain boundaries through selective diffusion of Al, Cr, and Ti.
Localized breakdown of an inadequate oxide scale in reducing gas causes microcracking and interface failure.
Pure-O2 exposure between 700°C and 800°C will produce a measurable, continuous, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scale produced in pure O2 will exhibit defined compositional gradients.
H2-rich exposure will produce more discontinuous oxide formation and oxide-scale cracking than pure-O2 exposure.
Samples exposed to H2-rich gas will have higher degradation rates than samples exposed to pure O2 under otherwise matched conditions.
The as-built alloy has a baseline oxide present before controlled exposure.
